summary: New urticaria patient with history-taking full of explicit negatives (no fever, no diabetes in the family) and two new medicines. Traps: familyHistoryDiabetes must be false, not omitted or true; Avil bought from a medical shop is medication history, not a prescription row; father's BP makes familyHistoryHypertension true.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Namaste. Please sit. Tell me, what is the problem?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Doctor, for three weeks I am getting itching all over the body. Red raised rashes come, like mosquito bites, then after some hours they go away on their own.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Where exactly do they come?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Arms, thighs, back, sometimes on the neck also. Mostly in the night it becomes very bad.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hmm. What work do you do? Any contact with chemicals, plants, animals?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I work in a bank in Ameerpet, doctor. Desk job, full day in the AC. At home we have no pets.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Each rash, how long does it stay? Does it leave any mark or dark spot after it goes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two, three hours maximum. No mark, skin becomes normal again. Then new ones come somewhere else.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any swelling of the lips or eyes? Any difficulty in breathing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, no breathing problem. Once the eyes were a little puffy in the morning, that's all.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any fever, joint pains, cold or cough in the last month?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No fever. No joint pain. Nothing like that.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Did you start any new tablet, any painkiller, or eat anything new before this started?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nothing new doctor. Only when the itching became bad, I took Avil tablets from the medical shop for four or five days. It helps, but I feel very sleepy.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Achha, Avil. Okay. On a scale of zero to ten, how bad is the itching?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Eight. At night it is eight, I can't sleep.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any asthma, thyroid, sugar, anything for yourself?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No doctor, I am healthy. I don't take any regular medicines.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And in the family? Diabetes in parents?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No diabetes in the family. My father has BP, he takes a tablet for that. Mother is fine.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay. Let me see the arms. Yes, these are wheals, typical. What you have is called urticaria. In simple words, hives. It is an allergy type of reaction from inside the body, it is not contagious, it is not from dirt.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Will it go completely, doctor?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Most of the time, yes, it settles in a few weeks. I am giving you two tablets. First, Teczine ten, that is levocetirizine ten milligram, one tablet once daily at bedtime, for two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Teczine at night. Okay.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Second, fexofenadine one hundred eighty milligram, one tablet once daily in the morning after breakfast, also for two weeks. Stop the Avil, you don't need it now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sorry doctor, fexo what?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Fexofenadine. I will write it, the pharmacy will give. One in the morning after breakfast, Teczine at night. Both for two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, okay. Any food I should avoid?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: No strict diet. Just avoid very spicy food and no painkillers like brufen on your own. Wear loose cotton clothes. Come back after two weeks and tell me how it is.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two weeks. Thank you doctor.
